Use REM Launcher as Default Home
Make REM Launcher your primary home screen for a more cinematic TV experience.
Active: the Home button opens REM Launcher.
Android gave REM the Home role, but this Google TV still sends the Home button to its own launcher. Turn on Home Redirect below.
This Google TV reserves the Home button for its own launcher, so Android can\'t switch it. Turn on Home Redirect below instead.
Off. Press OK to choose REM Launcher as your Home app.
Off. Press Home on your remote and pick REM Launcher if Android asks.
Opens REM whenever Google TV\'s home screen would appear: after Home, after leaving an app, and at start-up. Google TV stays installed.
On: Home, leaving apps and start-up all land in REM. Press OK to turn it off.
Off. Press OK for the one-time setup.
Step-by-step help to make REM open with the Home button.
Visit the original home screen. Home Redirect pauses until you reopen REM, or for 10 minutes.
Clear defaults or uninstall REM Launcher.

• Arrows move, OK opens, Back goes back. Menu (☰) opens Settings.
• Up from the content reaches Home, Video, Music, Apps and Settings.
• Google TV stays installed and untouched; Settings → Go to Google TV home takes you there.

Want REM to open with the Home button? Choose Set up Home.

This Google TV keeps its own launcher on the Home button, even for apps that hold Android's Home role. REM can take over safely with its Home Redirect:

1 Press OK on Open Accessibility settings below.
2 Choose REM Home Redirect, switch it on and confirm.
3 Press Back. Home, leaving an app and start-up now all land in REM.

Greyed out as a "restricted setting"? Open App info, press the menu (⋮) and choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Nothing is disabled or uninstalled. Switch it off here or in Accessibility at any time.
This device lets you choose your Home app. Press Choose Home app, pick REM Launcher and confirm. To undo it later, choose Google TV again or clear REM\'s defaults in App info.

Opens REM Launcher whenever the Google TV home screen comes to the front. It is only told when that one screen appears, reads no screen content and changes nothing else. Turn it off to restore the original behaviour.
